title: Studio form predicates: a parenthesised visibleWhen fails open, so the field editor shows percent and currency rows on every field type
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyUSf2nKJWW6qBemSU

Filing gate: ① (b) out-of-scope finding from the #36799 card thread's pre-claim measurement (`/mnt/project-files/card-36799/pre-claim-report-815e882b.md`, finding A), reproduced on origin/main 815e882b. Source: fleet.

## 维护者速读

- 问题：Studio 表单的显示条件（visibleWhen）一带括号就失效，变成「总是显示」。结果是字段编辑器在所有字段类型上都显示「百分比显示」和「货币」两行，管理员在文本字段上也能看到并填写这些不相关的选项。
- 修法：让 Studio 的求值器支持括号分组，并且在读不懂一个条件时默认隐藏、不默认显示。两种修法（改求值器，或者把表单里的条件改成不带括号）由开发实测后在卡上说明。
- 优先级 p2：每个打开字段编辑器的管理员都会碰到。

## Measured (origin/main 815e882b)

- The evaluator is `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/predicate.ts`. A `(…)` group's left side is read as the path `(data`, which throws `UnresolvedPathError`, and the predicate then answers **true**.
- `data.type == 'percent' || (data.type == 'formula' && data.returnType == 'percent')` on `{type:'text'}` evaluates **true**. The same sentence without the parentheses evaluates false.
- Rows affected today: `packages/spec/src/data/field.metadata-form.ts` `percentDisplay` (l.102) and the currency row (l.120). Both are offered on every field type.
- The forms declare `dialect: 'cel'`, and CEL allows parentheses, so a form author has no reason to avoid them.

## Ask

1. In `predicate.ts`, either support parenthesised grouping or refuse it, and make a predicate the evaluator cannot read fail **closed** (row hidden), not open. If the fix refuses parentheses, add a guard in `packages/spec` that no `*.metadata-form.ts` predicate uses a construct the evaluator does not read.
2. Pins for both affected `field.metadata-form.ts` rows on `text`, `percent`, and `formula` with returnType `percent`, plus one malformed predicate that must hide.

## Acceptance

- On a `text` field the editor no longer offers `percentDisplay` or the currency row. On `percent`, and on `formula` returning `percent`, it still offers them.
- An unreadable predicate hides its row. A pin turns red if the evaluator goes back to answering true.
- Related: #36799 writes its hook predicates without parentheses for this reason. Once this card lands, that workaround can stay as it is.
